purpose: Observed real geology references for native C++ rock, cliff, strata and talus math; photographs are not procedural texture inputs
license: USGS pages individually label each photograph Public Domain

references.observed: Many continuous cross-beds bend and truncate within a large sandstone mass; visible relief follows broad banding rather than isolated floating slabs.
references.playgroundGap: Preset 5 currently makes parallel, stacked contact slabs but no oblique internal foresets or truncation.

references.observed: Massive face with fine inclined laminations, cut joints and an undercut/ledge; bedding and fracture directions are distinct.
references.playgroundGap: The current cliff has directional relief but a wall-like outline; masks/normal detail cannot add structural joints or ledges.

references.observed: Vertical cooling columns below an irregular overhang, intersecting upper joints and broken angular fragments at the base.
references.playgroundGap: A basalt-column option would need aligned column joints and fallen contact pieces; the sedimentary cliff preset is not a basalt model.

references.observed: Broken blocks vary greatly in size and facet orientation and rest in a contact-filled talus slope, without broad air bands.
references.playgroundGap: Angular preset 10 is one clipped block, not a fractured pile; layered contact settling is only static first-contact placement.
